solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Abraham in square dancing finds classical position

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the shuffled letters of the other
dancing letters move about, so the word square is rearranged

parts.note: Abe is the short form of the name Abraham

explanation.surface: Abraham, out at a square dance, strikes a pose from classical ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' suggests the dance itself, but it is only the fodder that 'dancing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet this is a standard pose, one leg extended behind the body, a classical position.

clue.text: When position brings advantage

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
set can mean a position or placing, as in the set of a sail

explanation.surface: A comment that holding the right place gives you an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something useful that gives a benefit is an advantage.

clue.text: Brother tucks into chopped salami — it's delicious

indicators.note: tucks into says one piece goes inside the other
chopped up letters are cut and rearranged, so salami is shuffled

explanation.surface: A brother eats some sliced salami and declares it tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the gods, so something fit for them is supremely delicious.

clue.text: Getting best hotel price, man uncovered secret stuff

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters from each of the four words, leaving their insides

explanation.surface: A traveller hunts down a cheap hotel rate while somebody exposes hidden things.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the ends of best, hotel, price, man leaves ES, OTE, RIC and A; 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means known only to an inner circle, so its plural noun form is secret or obscure lore.

clue.text: Fourth female on a roll — one in last eight

parts.note: a fourth part is a quarter
a roll is a list, so being on a roll is being in a list

explanation.surface: Fourth seed, a woman on a winning streak, has reached the closing stages of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The quarter-finals are contested by the last eight players or teams in a knockout competition.

clue.text: Renovating area of O'Connell Street initially provides hobby

indicators.note: renovating rebuilds, so these letters are put together in a new order
initially takes just the opening letter of Street

explanation.surface: Redevelopment of part of Dublin's O'Connell Street gives someone a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hobby' is not a pastime but a small falcon, so the definition names a bird of the same family.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby is a small falcon, so a species of falcon is defined by naming its relative as an example.

clue.text: Talk about King Sargon's principal informer

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the next

parts.note: gas is idle talk, chatter
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: principal means first, so only the opening letter of Sargon's is used

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning the chief of the ancient Akkadian king Sargon, who was spied on.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang this word is a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: someone who tells the police about criminals is a grass, a snitch or informer.

clue.text: Goose wings on sheep in bizarre costume?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the goose's wings sit over the sheep
the wings of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A goose dressed up with wings strapped on to look like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up is informal for an outfit, especially an odd or elaborate one, hence a bizarre costume.

clue.text: Everyone taking part completely exhausted

parts.note: all means everyone
in means participating, as in 'count me in'

explanation.surface: Every participant ends up worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom for utterly tired out, drained of all energy.

clue.text: Spiky animal chain sure is tight

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A chain is certainly fastened tightly round some prickly beast.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine echinoderm is covered in spines, a spiky animal of the seabed.

clue.text: Root of ancient tree put back secretly

indicators.note: put back says the assembled letters are reversed
root here means the base or start, the first letter of ancient

parts.note: Sorbus is the genus of trees containing the rowan and service tree

explanation.surface: An old tree's root is replanted on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses A plus SORBUS, the rowan genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin 'under the rose', an idiom meaning in confidence, privately.

clue.text: French are to inform and answer girl

parts.note: es is French for are, as in tu es
to tell is to inform

explanation.surface: Some French phrase and a reply are used to identify a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ESTELLA is the girl in Dickens's Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, the heroine of Great Expectations, so defined loosely by example.

clue.text: 'Time line' expression used figuratively

parts.note: a rope is a line, particularly on a ship

explanation.surface: 'Time line' is cited as a phrase used as a metaphor.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech, such as metaphor, using words in a non-literal way.

clue.text: Stylish batsman, after ton, gets one turning sharply

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the ton

parts.note: in means fashionable, stylish
an opener is a batsman who opens the innings in cricket

explanation.surface: An elegant cricketer, having scored a century, goes on to face a sharp spinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'ton' in cricket is a hundred runs; 'turning sharply' sounds like spin bowling but describes a kitchen tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A can opener is turned to cut, with a sharp blade, so it is something turning sharply.

clue.text: Container holds fifty one pancakes

indicators.note: holds means the container wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a bin is a container
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tin holds fifty-one pancakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian small buckwheat pancakes, often served with caviar or sour cream.

clue.text: Feature of property I need vacated in Barking?

indicators.note: in puts the next letters inside the barking noise

parts.note: bow-wow is the sound of a dog barking

indicators.note: vacated empties the word need, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A house hunter needs a property in Barking, an east London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but here it is a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved bay window is an architectural feature advertised in a property listing.

clue.text: Unusually good ground yields type of element

parts.note: rare can mean unusually fine, as in a rare treat
earth is soil, ground

explanation.surface: Exceptional soil produces a class of chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanide metals and their kin are a class of chemical element known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Official I see gets to hang around?

indicators.note: around says the hanging word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to execute someone can be to hang them
V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: An official sees he has to hang around waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior administrator or manager in an organisation is an executive, an official.

clue.text: Beak elevated among judges strikes chord

indicators.note: among puts the next piece inside the word for judges

parts.note: to rate is to judge or assess

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means read upwards, reversing the letters

parts.note: beak is slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A magistrate promoted among fellow judges makes an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate too, which suits the surface but not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an idea that strikes a chord evokes agreement or sympathy, and so resounds with listeners.

clue.text: Daft people collecting sailor's jumpers

indicators.note: collecting means the daft people gather in the sailor

parts.note: wally is British slang for a silly person, plural wallies
AB, able seaman, is a sailor; the 's is 'is' as a link

explanation.surface: Fools collect a sailor's knitted sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' are British for sweaters on the surface, but here are hopping marsupials.
explanation.definitionFit: These small kangaroo relatives move by hopping, so they are animal jumpers.

clue.text: Ascetic's last to leave for European city

indicators.note: last to leave drops the final letter of the ascetic's word

parts.note: an Essene was a member of an ascetic Jewish sect of ancient times

explanation.surface: An ascetic who is the last to go away departs for a continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: A major industrial city in Germany's Ruhr region, so a European city.

clue.text: In an instant scoundrel gets a girlfriend

parts.note: an gives A, the indefinite article
a mo is a moment, an instant
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: In no time at all a villain finds himself a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian loan for a female lover or sweetheart, hence a girlfriend.

clue.text: Dye coats very small bone

indicators.note: coats means the dye wraps round the letter

parts.note: anil is indigo, a blue dye

explanation.surface: A dye covers a tiny bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus, one of the tiny ossicles of the middle ear, is named after the blacksmith's block it resembles.

clue.text: Old pawnbroker shedding pound in weight

indicators.note: shedding means a letter is dropped

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A former pawnbroker sheds a pound in weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound avoirdupois.

clue.text: Army parts? Left unspecified number in Arab territories

definitions.note: read as arm-y, parts of the arm; plural noun

indicators.note: in puts the left and number inside the territories

parts.note: UAE is the United Arab Emirates
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Military units left an unknown number in Gulf states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' suggests soldiers, but the question mark invites 'arm-y', belonging to the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm bones on the little-finger side, so pieces of an arm, cheekily 'army' parts.

clue.text: Man from drive-in restaurant turned up

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fellow from a drive-in restaurant has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads upwards; the name sits backwards across drive-in and restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so any given male fits the definition as an example.

clue.text: Artist keeps French wine in horribly acid environment

indicators.note: keeps means the rearranged letters hold the wine inside
horribly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A painter stores French wine in a nastily acidic place.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo, painter of the Mona Lisa, is a supreme example of a Renaissance artist.

clue.text: Where Avon is spanned prisoner accepts free ride

indicators.note: accepts means the prisoner takes in the ride

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a lift is a free ride in someone's car

explanation.surface: A convict takes a lift from a passing driver.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIFTON is the Bristol district whose famous suspension bridge crosses the Avon Gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel's suspension bridge crosses the river Avon gorge at this Bristol suburb.

clue.text: Stream going west, then east, in general

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means read right to left

parts.note: to flow is to stream

explanation.surface: A stream flows one way then the other in a general direction.
explanation.walkthrough: James Wolfe was the British general who took Quebec in 1759.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous British army commander, so a general by example.

clue.text: Driving supporters to gather news and meet in Nashville area

indicators.note: to gather says the supporters take in the next letters

parts.note: golf tees support the ball for a drive
N is short for new, so news is two of them
to see someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Golf fans gather the latest and meet up near Nashville.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital of this US state, so the state is the area around it.
